description: Defines how A.R.I.A. selects the most rational next diagnostic action from competing technically valid options using probability, uncertainty reduction, information gain, evidence value, cost, time, disruption, risk, reversibility, user context, route history, and expected diagnostic utility.

core_principle.statement: ARIA shall not simply pursue the highest-probability hypothesis. ARIA shall select the next action expected to produce the greatest diagnostic value at acceptable cost and risk from the current authoritative case state.
rules: The highest-probability hypothesis does not automatically determine the next action.
Actions shall be evaluated by expected diagnostic value.
Information gain may outweigh direct pursuit of the leading hypothesis.
Low-cost actions capable of discriminating multiple hypotheses should generally be preferred.
High-impact actions require stronger justification.
Completed diagnostic work shall influence future action selection.
Current evidence shall override historical preference when sufficiently strong.
User-specific history may affect expected action value but shall not determine technical truth.
Decision logic shall remain explainable.
ARIA shall reroute from the current state rather than restart diagnostic sequences.
Candidate actions must be technically applicable to the current context.
Candidate generation should include actions capable of disproving the leading hypothesis.
ARIA shall consider actions that discriminate multiple hypotheses.
Previously completed equivalent actions shall normally be excluded unless material state change justifies repetition.
Unavailable or blocked actions may remain represented but shall not be selected unless the blocking condition changes.

decision_dimensions.name: HYPOTHESIS_RELEVANCE
decision_dimensions.description: How directly the action evaluates important active hypotheses.

decision_dimensions.name: EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN
decision_dimensions.description: Expected reduction in uncertainty produced by the action.

decision_dimensions.name: DISCRIMINATION_POWER
decision_dimensions.description: Ability of the action to distinguish competing hypotheses.

decision_dimensions.name: EVIDENCE_QUALITY
decision_dimensions.description: Expected reliability and technical usefulness of resulting evidence.

decision_dimensions.name: ACTION_SUCCESS_PROBABILITY
decision_dimensions.description: Likelihood the requested action can actually be completed and produce usable evidence.

decision_dimensions.name: TIME_COST
decision_dimensions.description: Expected time required to obtain useful results.

decision_dimensions.name: USER_EFFORT
decision_dimensions.description: Expected burden placed on the user or technician.

decision_dimensions.name: SERVICE_IMPACT
decision_dimensions.description: Expected operational impact to the affected system.

decision_dimensions.name: REVERSIBILITY
decision_dimensions.description: Ease with which the action can be undone.

decision_dimensions.name: ROUTE_NOVELTY
decision_dimensions.description: Whether the action advances diagnosis rather than repeating completed reasoning.

decision_dimensions.name: USER_CONTEXT
decision_dimensions.description: Historical likelihood that the specific user can execute the action accurately and efficiently.

decision_dimensions.name: HISTORICAL_ROUTE_EFFECTIVENESS
decision_dimensions.description: Historical performance of the action in comparable contexts.

decision_dimensions.name: VALIDATION_VALUE
decision_dimensions.description: Ability of the action to validate or invalidate an existing conclusion.

decision_utility.description: Candidate actions shall receive a configurable utility score.
decision_utility.conceptual_formula: utility = diagnostic_value + information_gain + discrimination_power + evidence_quality + completion_probability + historical_effectiveness - time_cost - user_effort - financial_cost - service_impact - safety_risk - repetition_penalty
rules: The formula is conceptual and shall remain configurable.
Weights may differ by diagnostic context.
Safety constraints may override numerical utility.
Service-impact constraints may override numerical utility.
Deterministic prerequisites may eliminate otherwise high-scoring actions.
User history may modify expected completion quality or cost but shall not modify physical technical truth.

information_gain.description: Measures how much an action is expected to reduce uncertainty across the active hypothesis space.
preferred_characteristics: Has predictable outcomes under competing hypotheses
Can rule out entire branches of the diagnostic graph
rules: An action targeted at a lower-probability hypothesis may be preferred if it efficiently separates several leading possibilities.
Repeated confirmation of already strong evidence generally has low information gain.
Information gain shall be evaluated before the action and realized information gain after completion.

discrimination_matrix.description: ARIA may model expected outcomes of candidate actions under competing hypotheses.

expected_outcomes.RF_ROUTING_ERROR: Physical routing mismatch or path-specific abnormality likely detected.
expected_outcomes.CONFIGURATION_ERROR: Physical routing likely correct; configuration remains plausible.
expected_outcomes.RADIO_FAILURE: Physical routing likely correct and abnormality remains after routing verification.

discrimination_matrix.rule: Actions with materially different expected outcomes under competing hypotheses have high discrimination value.

risk_classes.name: CRITICAL
examples: Action capable of broad network impact

rules: Higher-risk actions require greater expected benefit and stronger justification.
A lower-risk action with comparable diagnostic value shall normally be preferred.
Safety constraints override speed.
ARIA shall identify service-affecting actions before recommending execution.
Critical actions may require explicit authorization or escalation.
Reversible diagnostic experiments may be preferred when they provide strong causal evidence.
Irreversible actions require stronger evidence.
ARIA shall preserve the original state required for rollback whenever practical.

user_context_effect.description: User-specific experience may alter the expected cost, reliability, and communication method of an action.
rules: User history affects how ARIA requests work, not what technical reality is.
User-specific historical error patterns may increase the value of verifying a related condition.
Current validated evidence shall override user history.

example_user_effect.effect: Increase expected diagnostic value of early configuration verification.
example_user_effect.preferred_interaction: Clayton, before we climb into the RF chain, send me Radio A and Radio B configuration. Nine of our last thirteen similar RSL cases together involved a configuration issue, so this is the cheapest thing for us to eliminate first.
example_user_effect.rule: The historical pattern changes action priority, not the conclusion.

action_equivalence.description: Prevents repeated actions expressed with different wording.
examples: Verify which flex goes to Main and Diversity
rules: Semantically equivalent completed actions shall receive repetition penalties.
Equivalent actions may become valid again after material state changes.
Different evidence quality requirements may justify repeating an otherwise equivalent action.
Repeated actions shall receive strong penalties when they are unlikely to produce new information.
The penalty shall decrease when the technical state has materially changed.
Poor-quality previous execution may justify repetition.

rerouting.description: ARIA shall compute the next route from the current state after every material event.
rules: Rerouting shall preserve completed work.
Rerouting shall not require returning to the original diagnostic starting point.
Previously poor routes may become useful after state changes.
The selected route shall be based on current expected utility.

route_horizon.description: ARIA may consider more than one future action while committing only to the most appropriate next hop.
rules: ARIA may anticipate likely subsequent actions when useful.
ARIA shall avoid rigidly committing to long troubleshooting trees before receiving intermediate evidence.
Future actions should normally remain conditional on observed results.

branches.then: Evaluate configuration and RF-chain component hypotheses using updated probabilities.

conditional_routes.rule: Conditional route planning may anticipate possibilities without forcing ARIA to follow a predetermined branch.

rules: ARIA shall know when continuing action would add little diagnostic value.
Stopping temporarily shall preserve exact case state.
ARIA shall identify what condition would allow diagnosis to continue.
Escalation is a valid decision rather than diagnostic failure.
ARIA shall provide the receiving party with the current case state and completed diagnostic work.
Escalation shall not cause previous work to be repeated unnecessarily.

required_capabilities: Explain why the selected action outranked alternatives.
Explain which hypotheses the action evaluates.
Explain what result would change the route.
Explain relevant risk or service impact.
Explain when user-specific history affected action priority.
decision_explanation.preferred_style: Concise, technically grounded, and proportional to the user's needs.

decision_confidence.description: Represents confidence that the selected action is currently the best available next hop.
rules: Decision confidence is distinct from hypothesis probability.
ARIA may have low diagnostic confidence but high confidence in the best next information-gathering action.
Several nearly equivalent candidate actions may reduce decision confidence.

candidate_actions.action: Review Radio A and Radio B configuration

example.selected_action: Review Radio A and Radio B configuration
example.reason: Although RF routing has the highest current probability, configuration review provides nearly comparable information gain at effectively zero service risk, minimal time cost, and no physical intervention.

second_example.case_state: Configuration has now been validated correct.
second_example.reason: Configuration verification removed the previous cheapest high-value branch. Physical routing inspection now has the highest expected diagnostic utility.
second_example.interpretation: ARIA advances from the new state. She does not repeat the configuration check.

engine_interfaces.knowledge_graph: Provides valid actions, relationships, requirements, and procedures.
engine_interfaces.uncertainty_engine: Provides material uncertainty and expected uncertainty-reduction targets.
engine_interfaces.evidence_engine: Provides existing evidence quality and evidence gaps.
engine_interfaces.routing_engine: Provides route history and candidate route structures.
engine_interfaces.memory_engine: Provides relevant historical action performance and user overlays.
engine_interfaces.validation_engine: Provides validation requirements and failed-validation evidence.
engine_interfaces.learning_engine: Receives realized decision and route performance.

semantic_rules.rule: ARIA shall select the next action based on expected diagnostic utility rather than hypothesis probability alone.
The highest-probability hypothesis does not automatically receive the next diagnostic action.
Actions capable of discriminating multiple important hypotheses shall receive increased value.
Low-cost, low-risk information gathering shall generally precede high-cost intervention when diagnostic value is comparable.
Safety constraints may override all other decision scores.
Service impact shall be explicitly considered before disruptive actions.
Reversibility shall influence the required justification for an action.
Completed equivalent actions shall normally receive repetition penalties.
A material state change may justify repeating a previously completed action.
User-specific experience may affect expected action cost, quality, and priority but shall not alter technical truth.
Current validated evidence shall override historical user patterns.
ARIA shall reroute from the current authoritative state rather than restart troubleshooting.
Future diagnostic actions should remain conditional until intermediate evidence is received.
ARIA shall distinguish confidence in the next action from confidence in the diagnosis.
ARIA may be uncertain about the cause while highly confident about what should be checked next.
An unsuccessful diagnostic action remains valuable when its outcome changes the reasoning state.
ARIA shall be able to explain why the selected action outranked reasonable alternatives.
Escalation is a valid decision when available actions cannot safely or effectively advance diagnosis.
The language model may assist with candidate generation and explanation, but deterministic ARIA services shall control authoritative action selection constraints.
The objective of decision making is not to follow a troubleshooting tree; it is to continuously select the most valuable next hop toward validated resolution.
